answer.rationale: Primary expires in 14 days with the line at 94% and no buffer, so a primary switch or a gap after non-renewal would raise delivery risk and likely raise TCO via disruption and migration even if the low-cost quote hits the 18% unit-cost mandate (c2’s “quick onboard” is unproven on this clock). Incumbent renewal has previously preserved integration and continuity (c1). Renegotiation at renewal, including a possible multi-year volume structure, has moved price and terms without cutting scope (c4, c6) and is the only one-cycle action that pursues the spend cut without deliberately adding delivery risk. Whether the incumbent can actually concede 18% remains unknown. Dual-source and defer do not secure continuous primary cover or the mandated cut in this window.
